firmwares.name: Makkuro37
firmwares.author: genkigenki
firmwares.about: A microtonal drone synth: eight voices as eight soot creatures, 96 presets.

firmwares.name: Vector37
firmwares.author: genkigenki
firmwares.about: An orbiting overtone synth: a moon circles a sun along a path, and where it is decides how much of each of four sounds you hear.

firmwares.name: Speak37
firmwares.author: genkigenki
firmwares.about: A talking synth for the SMK-37 and the FM-1: every key speaks the next word at its pitch, chords speak in harmony. And MOPE, a gloomy robot who listens to what you play and tells you what he thinks of it.

firmwares.name: Erik37
firmwares.author: genkigenki
firmwares.about: A grand piano for the SMK-37: a sampled concert grand with velocity layers, dampers and their noise, the three pedals, string resonance and four rooms.

firmwares.name: Snoop37
firmwares.author: isod89
firmwares.about: SLOOP, the four-track looper groovebox, adapted for the SMK-37.

firmwares.name: X0X
firmwares.author: Charles Vestal
firmwares.about: A 909, an 808, two 303s with a line generator and a breakbeat player, all at once.

firmwares.name: FoMni
firmwares.author: Charles Vestal
firmwares.about: An Omnichord-style chord harp: the 16 pads become the strum plate, the keybed holds the chords.

firmwares.name: MAKU
firmwares.author: okumurari2
firmwares.about: An always-on ambience machine: power it on and a new, random, in-key world is already playing.

firmwares.name: Rainbow mode
firmwares.author: joshbartlettband-web
firmwares.about: A music toy for kids: colour-coded notes, 40 friends who sing along, no menus.

firmwares.name: GHOULBOX
firmwares.author: Jason Persinger
firmwares.about: Dungeon-synth firmware: dark ambient, medieval and fantasy sounds, with drones, a hurdy-gurdy crank and two sounds at once.

firmwares.name: ChoralRoot
firmwares.author: Quixotic7, with the SMK-37 stock-mapping fix (PR #22)
firmwares.about: A chord instrument in the manner of the Orchid: one hand plays roots, the other picks the chord.

firmwares.name: ORBIT
firmwares.author: dspaudio
firmwares.about: A four-track groovebox with OP-1-inspired screens: three synth parts, a drum machine, an event tape and a mixer.

firmwares.name: AMB-1
firmwares.author: Charles Vestal
firmwares.about: A generative ambient machine inspired by Music for Airports: loops of different lengths drift past each other and never repeat.

firmwares.name: Polly
firmwares.author: Charles Vestal
firmwares.about: A pocket arranger inspired by the Yamaha QY70: a band of eight General MIDI instruments follows the chords you play.

firmwares.name: winampFM
firmwares.author: Hericdk
firmwares.about: A synth groovebox in the look of Winamp 2.x, built on SLOOP: player, playlist, effect sliders and a visualizer.

firmwares.name: DUB-1
firmwares.author: sbegueria
firmwares.about: A generative dub techno machine: chord stabs through a low-pass into a tape echo, a sub bass, a kick that ducks the rest. You don't play it, you steer it.

firmwares.name: Ketch
firmwares.author: Adrien Risser-Zhuang
firmwares.about: A tracker in the LSDJ / M8 line: song, chain and phrase screens, Felucca's sound engines on four channels, effects and a mixer.

firmwares.name: Melodee
firmwares.author: keremimo
firmwares.about: A four-track multi-engine synth and sequencer: Prophet, CZ, FM6, SID, drums and more.

firmwares.name: FMEL-1
firmwares.author: AntonioAltea, on zvenson's Dinghy
firmwares.about: A Mellotron M400 in your SMK-37: real tapes, wow and flutter, a second sound on the other track. The tapes are Bernie Kornowicz's (Taijiguy) M400S samples: free to use, never in anything sold.

firmwares.name: Frodhes
firmwares.author: Leonardo Mirabal, on zvenson's Dinghy
firmwares.about: A physically modelled electric piano: every note computed live from a hammer, a tine and a pickup. Four instrument types, a compressor, tremolo, phaser, chorus, delay and reverb.

firmwares.name: ZEN-1
firmwares.author: aceyprime, on FuMi-1 and FoMni
firmwares.about: Ambient scenes that play themselves: a cherry tree over a stream, a koi pond, fireflies under a real moon. Every movement on screen is a note, on a 6-operator FM engine.

firmwares.name: OberVave
firmwares.author: zvenson
firmwares.about: One 8-voice analog-style polysynth in the spirit of the American poly synths of 1979–84, with chorus, delay and a plate reverb.
